samples.summary: §4 reads pooled panel series (`review_cost_usd`, `review_wall_ms`, `latency_interval`) that the only producer of `cost-latency-v1` never emits — every headline row will render "not computed" on a real store
samples.evidence: Consumer: report.mjs:660-676 reads `panel.replicate_spend_usd` (exists), but also `panel.review_cost_usd`, `panel.review_wall_ms` and `panel.latency_interval`. Producer `costLatencyOf` at scripts/agent/eval/cost-latency.mjs:666-680 emits only `{unit, replicates, per_item, by_size_bucket, replicate_spend_usd, duration_source}` — the per-review cost/wall series live PER REPLICATE as `replicates[].review.cost_usd` / `.review.wall_ms` (cost-latency.mjs:407-421), and no `latency_interval` string exists anywhere in that file (grep for `review_wall_ms|review_cost_usd|latency_interval` in cost-latency.mjs: no matches). So against the 32 KB payload the follow-up doc says is sitting in `scores/`, `cost per review` and `wall clock per review` both take the `notComputed("the cost score carries no pooled …series")` branch, and the section that was written to publish those minutes publishes nothing. Only the invented fixture at report.test.mjs:140-143 makes them render.

samples.summary: `fitCell` requires `cost_vs_size.min_n`, which `fitCostToSize` never emits — a withheld fit renders as permanently `not-measurable` instead of `suppressed`, mislabelling a re-runnable gap as structural
samples.evidence: `fitCell` (report.mjs, new helper) does `if (Number.isFinite(fit.min_n) && fit.n < fit.min_n) return suppressed(...)`. The producer `fitCostToSize` at scripts/agent/eval/cost-latency.mjs:254 returns `{n, intercept_usd: null, slope_usd_per_1000_lines: null, fixed_share: null, reason: "a floor-plus-slope fit needs at least 3 items, got N"}` — no `min_n` key, and no `MIN_FIT_ITEMS` constant exists in the repo (grep: only report.test.mjs mentions the name, in a comment). So on a real payload the thin-fit path falls through to `notMeasurable(fit.reason)`, i.e. the report tells the reader a fit is permanently impossible when three more priced items would produce it — the exact conflation the module claims to prevent. The `suppressed` state for §4 is only reachable via the fixture (report.test.mjs:578).

samples.evidence: `renderLatencyLimit` returns `[]` unless `s.coderabbit.latency.availability === "present"` (report.mjs:1417-1418). verdict.reason: Verified independently. Consumer is present as described: report.mjs:664-666 reads `cr.latency.self_timed`/`push_proxy`, report.mjs:711-719 builds `latency`/`latency_secondary`/`triggers` cells, and report.mjs:1261-1281 renders the CodeRabbit latency row plus the trigger paragraph from them. This is an in-lane blast-radius contract mismatch (new required fields the existing producer does not supply); no guard or alternate producer refutes it.
